data.title: Hold Rating Reflects Softer Trading and Execution Risks Despite Higher Price Target
data.description:
Jamie Rollo, an analyst from Morgan Stanley, maintained the Hold rating on Mitchells & Butlers. The associated price target is p350.00.

Jamie Rollo has given his Hold rating due to a combination of softer trading, cautious forecasts and unresolved risks. Like-for-like sales growth slowed to 1.1%, while weaker restaurant performance and reduced pricing momentum led him to lower expectations for comparable sales and EBIT. However, lower interest costs largely offset the operating revisions, leaving earnings-per-share estimates broadly stable.
Cost pressures are easing, but energy exposure remains significant and could weaken profits if unhedged prices rise. Operational savings should provide support, while further deleveraging prompted a higher price target; nevertheless, uncertainty around near-term margins and the timing of shareholder returns limits the case for a stronger recommendation. This balance of modest earnings growth and material execution risks supports a Hold rather than a Buy.

data.title: Buy Rating Reaffirmed as Livsayis Approval and Pipeline Potential Drive Price Target Raise to $1,104
data.description:
Tazeen Ahmad, an analyst from Bank of America Securities, reiterated the Buy rating on Regeneron. The associated price target was raised to $1,104.00.

Tazeen Ahmad has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, led by Livsayis’s approval for AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis and supportive Phase 3 results. Its quarterly subcutaneous administration could distinguish it in a crowded complement-inhibitor market, encouraging adoption among patients seeking a more convenient alternative. The expanding biologics market and expected early-December availability also support the launch outlook.

Ahmad sees additional upside if Livsayis gains broader first-line use beyond patients switching from FcRn therapies. Ongoing studies in PNH and geographic atrophy provide further pipeline optionality for cemdisiran. The model anticipates approximately $1.2 billion in peak gMG sales, while the price objective was raised from $1,030 to $1,104, reinforcing the positive valuation view.

According to TipRanks, Ahmad is a 4-star analyst with an average return of 4.8% and a 57.17% success rate. Ahmad covers the Healthcare sector, focusing on stocks such as Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Argenx Se, and BioNTech SE.

In another report released on November 18, BMO Capital also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $1,050.00 price target.

data.title: Rogers Sugar: Hold as Stable Outlook and Limited Near-Term Catalysts Offset Sound Demand
data.description:
Analyst Stephen Macleod of BMO Capital maintained a Hold rating on Rogers Sugar, with a price target of C$7.50.

Stephen Macleod has given his Hold rating due to a combination of factors, including results that were broadly consistent with expectations and an outlook suggesting limited change in performance during 2027. Sugar operations face modest volume pressure, the reversal of temporary margin benefits, competitive domestic conditions, and weaker export demand, while Maple Products is expected to deliver largely stable volumes and profitability.
Although underlying sweetener demand remains sound and the dividend may appeal to income-focused investors, these positives appear largely reflected in Rogers Sugar’s current valuation. The company also faces uncertainty from U.S. trade negotiations and possible tariff-related effects, while the LEAP project will not be completed until 2027 and requires a longer ramp-up, limiting near-term catalysts.

data.title: Salesforce’s AI Expansion and Accelerating Growth Support Buy Rating; Price Target Unchanged at $266
data.description:

New offerings such as AIforce, along with integrations involving Microsoft and Slack, could help the company capture demand as customers build more agent-driven operations. He also points to a substantial acquisition program that broadens Salesforce’s capabilities and market reach.
